name: Denitrification Pathway
notes: Denitrification pathways using nitrogen oxides as terminal electron acceptors. Follows Stein 2016 nomenclature: Step 5 (NO3- → NO2-), Step 6A (NO2- → NO), Step 6B (NO → N2O), Step 6C (N2O → N2). Note: Step 5 is shared with DNRA, anammox, and nitrification. n-DAMO pathway (direct NO → N2 via nitric oxide dismutase in Candidatus Methylomirabilis oxyfera) is not included. Step 5 can be performed by either membrane-bound (narGHI) or periplasmic (napAB) nitrate reductase.

genes.name: nitrate reductase / nitrite oxidoreductase, alpha subunit
genes.notes: Membrane-bound nitrate reductase alpha subunit. Also involved in nitrification (reverse reaction).

genes.name: nitrate reductase / nitrite oxidoreductase, beta subunit
membrane-bound nitrate reductase complex
genes.notes: Three-subunit membrane-bound nitrate reductase. Alternative to periplasmic napAB system.

genes.name: nitrate reductase (cytochrome)
genes.notes: Periplasmic nitrate reductase catalytic subunit. Alternative to narGHI.

genes.name: nitrate reductase (cytochrome), electron transfer subunit
genes.notes: Periplasmic nitrate reductase electron transfer subunit.

genes.name: periplasmic nitrate reductase complex
genes.notes: Two-subunit periplasmic nitrate reductase. Alternative to membrane-bound narGHI system.

genes.name: nitrite reductase (NO-forming)
genes.notes: Copper-containing nitrite reductase. Alternative to nirS. Diagnostic marker for denitrification.

genes.name: nitrite reductase (NO-forming) / hydroxylamine reductase
genes.notes: Cytochrome cd1 nitrite reductase. Alternative to nirK. Diagnostic marker for denitrification.

genes.name: nitric oxide reductase subunit B
genes.notes: Catalytic subunit of nitric oxide reductase.

genes.name: nitric oxide reductase subunit C
genes.notes: Electron transfer subunit of nitric oxide reductase.

genes.name: nitric oxide reductase complex
genes.notes: Two-subunit NO reductase. Reduces NO to N2O.

genes.name: nitrous-oxide reductase
genes.notes: Reduces N2O to N2. Final step of complete denitrification. Organisms lacking nosZ release N2O (greenhouse gas).

complete_denitrification.name: Complete Denitrification (Steps 5+6A+6B+6C)
complete_denitrification.notes: Full canonical denitrification: NO3- → NO2- → NO → N2O → N2. All four steps present. Relatively uncommon - most organisms have partial pathways. nirK/nirS are diagnostic markers.

scoring.notes: Requires complete route from nitrate to N2. Gap-based scoring ensures all steps present.

incomplete_denitrification.name: Incomplete Denitrification (Steps 5+6A+6B, no 6C)
incomplete_denitrification.notes: NO3- → NO2- → NO → N2O (lacks nosZ). Very common. Releases N2O greenhouse gas. Major climate concern. nirK/nirS are diagnostic markers.

scoring.notes: Requires complete route to N2O but specifically LACKS nosZ. Use presence pattern to distinguish from complete denitrifiers.

n2o_sink.name: N2O Sink (Step 6C only)
n2o_sink.notes: N2O → N2. Organisms with just nosZ that consume environmental N2O. Ecologically important for climate mitigation. NOTE: Complete denitrifiers also score positive for this pathway (nested subset).

scoring.notes: Single gene pathway. Includes specialists (just nosZ) AND complete denitrifiers (have all genes). Check pathway membership table to distinguish.

nitrite_denitrification.name: Nitrite Denitrification (Steps 6A+6B+6C, no 5)
nitrite_denitrification.notes: NO2- → NO → N2O → N2. Starts from nitrite instead of nitrate (lacks step 5 narGHI/napAB). Organisms rely on external nitrite or coupled with upstream NO3- reduction by other organisms. nirK/nirS are diagnostic markers.

scoring.notes: Requires complete route from nitrite to N2. Specifically LACKS narGHI/napAB. Use presence pattern to distinguish from complete denitrifiers.
